 Plato: 

On Atlantis, from 
The Timaeus

Many great and wonderful deeds are recorded of your state in ourÂ histories. But one of them exceeds all the rest in greatness and valour.Â For these histories tell of a mighty power which unprovoked made an expeditionÂ against the whole of Europe and Asia, and to which your city put an end.Â This power came forth out of the Atlantic Ocean, for in those days theÂ Atlantic was navigable; and there was an island situated in front of theÂ straits which are by you called the Pillars of Heracles; the island wasÂ larger than Libya and Asia put together, and was the way to other islands,Â and from these you might pass to the whole of the opposite continent whichÂ surrounded the true ocean; for this sea which is within the Straits ofÂ Heracles is only a harbour, having a narrow entrance, but that other isÂ a real sea, and the surrounding land may be most truly called a boundlessÂ continent. Now in this island of Atlantis there was a great and wonderfulÂ empire which had rule over the whole island and several others, and overÂ parts of the continent, and, furthermore, the men of Atlantis had subjectedÂ the parts of Libya within the columns of Heracles as far as Egypt, andÂ of Europe as far as Tyrrhenia. This vast power, gathered into one, endeavouredÂ to subdue at a blow our country and yours and the whole of the region withinÂ the straits; and then, Solon, your country shone forth, in the excellenceÂ of her virtue and strength, among all mankind. She was pre-eminent in courageÂ and military skill, and was the leader of the Hellenes. And when the restÂ fell off from her, being compelled to stand alone, after having undergoneÂ the very extremity of danger, she defeated and triumphed over the invaders,Â and preserved from slavery those who were not yet subjugated, and generouslyÂ liberated all the rest of us who dwell within the pillars. But afterwardsÂ there occurred violent earthquakes and floods; and in a single day andÂ night of misfortune all your warlike men in a body sank into the earth,Â and the island of Atlantis in like manner disappeared in the depths ofÂ the sea. For which reason the sea in those parts is impassable and impenetrable,Â because there is a shoal of mud in the way; and this was caused by theÂ subsidence of the island.
